I recommend **recorded**: this is the same claim as one already on file. It is close to borderline, because I could not open the recorded files to compare wording.

**1. Page check: the words are on the page.** The Axios page opened. The quote is there word for word, including the bracketed "[world models, not LLMs]", which is Axios's insertion. This is a news report, not LeCun's own words. Axios says he said it "last month at a symposium at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, as noted in a Wall Street Journal profile." The article is dated 17 November 2025, so the words date to October 2025. Axios is quoting the Wall Street Journal second-hand, so on its own this source would be "pass, coverage only."

**2. The admission rule:**
- **Part 1 (role):** In October 2025 LeCun was still Meta's Chief AI Scientist. He left at the end of 2025, and Meta counts as a frontier-model company. Passes.
- **Part 2 (forward-looking and about AI):** It says world models will become the dominant AI architecture and that nobody sensible will use today's LLMs. That is a forecast about AI. It is not framed as a hypothetical. Passes.
- **Part 3 (date or span):** "Within three to five years" is a span. Taking the later end, it runs to October 2030, so the due year is 2030. Passes.
- **Part 4 (source):** Only coverage, and second-hand at that (Axios citing the WSJ citing an MIT talk). This gives "coverage only" at best, unless someone finds a recording or transcript of the MIT symposium.

**Why "recorded":** He frames this as a repeat himself: "I've been … saying that within three to five years…". It matches two recorded files from 23 January 2025: `llms-not-central-within-five-years` and `new-paradigm-in-three-to-five-years`. Both also come due in 2030 (January 2025 plus five years). Under the Restatements rule, a repeat with the same prediction and the same due year is not a new claim. It should be added as October 2025 in the `repeated_on` of the January claim. The person checking should confirm the January wording really matches, especially "nobody in their right mind would use" LLMs. If it differs in substance, this becomes a new claim, entered as "pass, coverage only."
